summary: Static review of commit a31a989 only; Playwright was not run, as instructed. All four round 1 findings are addressed correctly. (1) Helper move: a line diff of the lines removed from 0011 against the lines added to helpers.ts differs only by the added `export`. SORTABLE_SETTLE_MS and DRAG_AIM_ATTEMPTS moved with it, and no other file references them. helpers.ts already imports `Page` and `GroupId`. 0011 lost nothing but the function and the two constants. Its remaining `Page`/`GroupId` imports are still used, and both drag call sites (lines 490, 495) now resolve to the import. (2) AC-8 removes the first notice before the second completion and then asserts `toHaveCount(0)`. That is a real check of the second completion, with no dependency on the 5 s timeout. (3) AC-5 now enters completed with a real mouse drag, so it goes through Sortable `onEnd` (dataset.groupId read, the early-return guard, DOM revert) and on into moveTaskAndNotify. The store and notice assertions after the drag would fail if onEnd broke. The 1280x1400 viewport cannot leak into other tests: the page fixture is per test, and 0011 already uses the same pattern. The programmatic reorder check is kept. The note that programmatic entry into completed stays covered by AC-8 and the renamed-backlog AC-10 is accurate. (4) Both comments now match the code. The new AC-7 Decision 10 scenario is sound. The toast filter `hasText: 'Ship release'` matches only the complete toast, because delete toasts show the deleted task's `what` ('Run retro'). The flow of complete, expand, delete and Undo takes well under the 7 s toast lifetime. The asserted end state holds only if revertSpawnedFollowUps deletes the already-orphaned spawned task, and it does so via its `hasTask` / `delete data.tasks[id]` loop. The reported mutation check fits the code: without `dismissed.add(id)`, the delete toast survives and the count assertion fails. Not covered: the `clearTimeout` of dismissed toasts in handleUndo. It is not worth a finding, because the only effect of a stray expiry would be a delete of a task that is already gone. Committing the round 1 JSON into docs/features follows the existing convention (other task review JSONs there are tracked). No new findings.
